question: Should OpenClaw adopt this RFC’s core-wide localization governance, generated inventory, and fail-closed promotion-gate model as the sponsored direction for the dependency-ordered series?
rationale: The patch introduces a new shared package, public locale-selection behavior, repository-wide automation, and cross-surface ownership rules; code review cannot determine whether that product and maintenance commitment is wanted.

options.title: Sponsor the staged RFC rollout
options.body: Assign an owner to review and land the prerequisite bundles in order, with evidence and compatibility expectations defined for each boundary.

options.title: Narrow to current localization gaps
options.body: Reduce the work to a smaller, sponsored set of user-facing localization fixes and defer broad inventory and promotion governance.

options.title: Pause the series
options.body: Keep the draft open but do not advance the global governance and gate design until maintainers choose a localization strategy.

recommendation.title: Sponsor the staged RFC rollout
recommendation.body: Assign an owner to review and land the prerequisite bundles in order, with evidence and compatibility expectations defined for each boundary.

likelyOwner.reason: The author is the only evidence-backed routing contact for the documented series and RFC boundary; the actual sponsor must be a repository maintainer.
